reason: VALUE: the in-sample effect is real on 6bba but the finding oversells it, and the part that matters (transfer to unseen embryos) cannot be tested before R8. (1) At +0.1 vox only 14 of 56 clips change (11 up, 3 down), net +24 TP out of 40,093 GT edges, FP -47. The 44b6 +0.00251 rests on 2 clips: dropping e28840c6 gives +0.0009, dropping deabac95 gives +0.00145. The per-embryo bootstrap gives 44b6 P(<=0) = 0.13, so it would fail the finding's own 0.10 bar if applied per embryo. The 44b6 curve is jagged (+0.05 +0.0011, +0.1 +0.0025, +0.15 +0.0008, +0.2 -0.0003, +0.25 -0.0023), which is rounding and assignment noise, not a smooth bias correction. 6bba is solid (P(<=0) = 0, LOO min +0.00107, a plateau of +0.0015..+0.0018 over +0.1..+0.3). (2) The 6bba-calibrated quadratic (k ~0.0126 per um^2) predicts only +0.0003 for a 44b6-like bias of 0.15 um. The measured 44b6 value is about 8x inflated, and the honest per-embryo size is the OLD desk estimate (+0.0003..+0.0005). So the recheck corrects the old argument (the LB noise of 0.003 does not apply) but not the old number by much. (3) The bias depends on the embryo and the annotation, not on the pipeline: 44b6 +0.15 vs 6bba +0.45 um. The public head's mean z shift is ~-0.02 um, so it does not correct z. Canh sees ~0 vs 0.61 um, and his constant correction lost 0.0031 on the LB. The closed head-retrain kill test failed precisely on learning 6bba's z offset. A constant shift is the crudest form of that closed idea, and the 'smaller embryo bias' rule for c was chosen after seeing a ~9-shift lab grid. On a hidden embryo with bias <= 0 it loses: every negative offset loses in the lab, and 44b6 overshoot by ~0.3 um costs -0.0023. (4) Coordinate-only lab gains are 0 for 3 on the LB: floatout lab +0.0019..0.0025 tied on #32/#33, and Eric's sub-voxel refinement went +0.0078 local, -0.002 on the LB twice. FEASIBILITY/GATE: the patch itself is easy: default 0 skips the code (byte-identical), a try/except makes it fail-soft, runtime is ~0, and the schedule fits (now 10:41Z; the lab on ~40 clips takes ~1.3 h per shard by the exp60 kernel times 6,959/5,599 s; K7 could score by ~27 Sep 04Z). But the proposed 'honest bed' is not honest about the real risk. It re-measures the same two in-sample embryos, where the detector saw all 199 videos. Its 44b6 arm cannot be independent: exp60 already took one 44b6 clip from 17 of the 18 leak groups (the 18th is a head stem), so every other usable 44b6 clip shares GT annotations with a clip already measured. The only transfer read is one public score at 0.001 resolution, against an expected effect of ~+0.0003. The K7-vs-#37 choice would then be made on a public tie plus in-sample lab evidence, which is the near-copy choice R7 forbids outside R3, and R3 as written would admit K7 even at 0.953. Expected private gain is ~+0.0003 with a real chance of -0.0005..-0.001 on a low-bias embryo. That is not worth a finals change, new code, a GPU run and a slot 3 days before the deadline, with the finals already ticked.
fix: Do not replace #37 on this evidence. Record for the curator: I-041/I-029 are corrected, not reopened. The 'LB noise 0.003' argument is withdrawn (deterministic kernels), and the in-sample 6bba effect is real: +0.0015, P(<=0) = 0. But the transfer-adjusted value stays ~+0.0003, and the 44b6 +0.0025 is 2-clip noise (per-embryo P(<=0) = 0.13). Put it on the POST-DEADLINE list as a per-node or per-video learned z correction inside an embryo-held-out coordhead-v2, not as a constant. If the user still wants it before R8 (NEW OK required): (a) pre-register c = +0.1 with the per-embryo bootstrap rule P(<=0) < 0.10 on EACH embryo, not only ALL. (b) Take the 6bba bed from fresh stems (~77 available). For 44b6, state explicitly that the new clips are leak-group siblings, so that arm is a replication, not independent evidence. (c) Add a dummy check that max CSV z <= the base max z + 1 and that node and edge counts are identical to K2. (d) Make the pair decision explicit: {K7, #37} is a pure best-of hedge on the shift (max(K7, #37) >= #37) but drops the #38 insertion hedge. {K7, #38} spends the scored #37 on an effect the public score cannot resolve. The default is to keep {#37, #38}.
realistic_gain: Private ~+0.0003 (range -0.001..+0.0015); public 0 to +0.001, below the display resolution. The 6bba-like embryo is the upside; a hidden embryo with bias <= 0 (Canh's case) is the downside.
